title: Why seasons change
keyIdea: Through the year, the number of hours of daylight changes. In the UK, a day in June has about 16 and a half hours of daylight and a day in December has only about 8, but every day is still 24 hours long. The days get longer from winter to summer and shorter from summer to winter, again every year. Long days give more hours of sunshine, so summer is warmer and plants grow leaves; short winter days are colder.
familyTip: Keep a bedtime window diary. Once a week, look out at the same time, say 7 pm, and draw a sun or a moon on the calendar. After a few months, look back together: when did it start getting dark at bedtime? Ask: did bedtime change, or did the sunset change?

lab.caption: Flagship lab: bedtime light across the year, a June and a December day, months in order, a year chart and a tree.

kid: In summer, it can still be light at bedtime. In winter, it is dark before tea. Bedtime is the same. The Sun sets at a different time.
Every day is 24 hours long. But the light part changes. A June day has about 16 hours of light. A December day has only about 8.
From winter to summer, the days get longer. After June, they get shorter again. Then the pattern starts again, every year.
Long days give lots of sunshine. So summer is warm and trees are full of leaves. Short days give less sunshine. So winter is cold and many trees are bare.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This covers the Year 1 science aim in the National Curriculum in England to observe changes across the four seasons and how day length varies. It also covers NGSS 1-ESS1-2: relate the amount of daylight to the time of year. Key words: season, daylight, day length, sunrise, sunset, summer, winter.

The numbers use London clock times in the middle of each month. In mid-June the Sun rises about 4:45 am and sets about 9:20 pm, giving about 16 and a half hours of daylight. In mid-December it rises about 8 am and sets about 4 pm, giving about 8 hours. Further north the swing is bigger.

Common mistakes: thinking a winter day is shorter than 24 hours, rather than having fewer light hours; thinking summer is warm because the Sun is closer to the Earth, when the Earth is actually closest in early January; and thinking it is the same season everywhere. In Australia, December has the long days.

The real cause is the tilt of the Earth's axis, which children meet later. For now, the pattern is the goal. In the lab your child looks out at bedtime and fills in a June and a December day. They put four months in order of daylight and chart a whole year. Then they watch a tree and a thermometer change with the light.

practice.prompt: Why is it still light at bedtime in June?
choices: The Sun sets later in summer
The Sun is closer in June
practice.hint: Bedtime stays the same. What changes is when the Sun goes down.
practice.explain: In June the Sun sets after 9 o'clock in the evening, so it is still light at a 7 o'clock bedtime.

practice.prompt: A summer day has {a} hours of daylight. A winter day has {b}. How many more hours of daylight does the summer day have?
practice.hint: Take the winter hours away from the summer hours.
practice.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b}. The summer day has {=a-b} more hours of daylight.

practice.prompt: How long is a day in December?
choices: 24 hours, with only about 8 hours of light
Longer than a day in June
practice.hint: Think about the whole day, light part and dark part.
practice.explain: Every day is 24 hours. In December only about 8 of those hours are light; the rest are dark.

practice.prompt: A day is 24 hours. {a} hours are light. How many hours are dark?
practice.hint: Light hours and dark hours together make 24.

practice.prompt: After the long days of June, what happens?
practice.hint: Think of the year chart: up, then…
practice.explain: Daylight grows until June, then shrinks until December, then grows again. The pattern repeats every year.

pool.prompt: Which season has the longest days?
pool.hint: When can you play outside after dinner?
pool.explain: Summer has the longest days. In the UK, June days have about 16 and a half hours of daylight.

pool.prompt: Which month has the shortest days in the UK?
pool.hint: Think about the darkest, coldest time of year.
pool.explain: December has the shortest days, with only about 8 hours of daylight.

pool.prompt: From winter to summer, the days get…
pool.hint: Is it light earlier or later in the evening as summer comes?
pool.explain: Each month from December to June has more daylight than the one before.

choices: More hours of sunshine warm the land
The Sun is closer to us
pool.hint: Long days mean more of what?
pool.explain: Long days mean many hours of sunshine, which warm the ground and the air. It is not because the Sun is closer.

pool.prompt: Sam walks to school in the dark. Which month could it be?
pool.hint: When does the Sun rise late, after 7 o'clock?
pool.explain: In December the Sun rises about 8 o'clock, so an early walk to school is in the dark.

pool.prompt: The Sun rises at {a} o'clock in the morning and sets at {b} o'clock in the evening. How many hours of daylight is that?
pool.hint: Count the hours from sunrise up to 12 midday, then add the hours after midday.
pool.explain: From {a} o'clock to midday is {=12-a} hours. Then {b} more hours after midday. {=12-a} + {b} = {=12-a+b} hours of daylight.

pool.prompt: It is December. Is it summer in Australia?
choices: Yes, it has long days then
pool.hint: Australia is on the other side of the world.
pool.explain: The south half of the world has its seasons the other way round. December is summer in Australia.

pool.prompt: A winter day has {a} hours of light. A summer day has double that. How many hours of light does the summer day have?
pool.hint: Double means two lots of the same number.
pool.explain: {a} + {a} = {=2*a}. The summer day has {=2*a} hours of light.

pool.prompt: What do many trees look like in winter, when days are short?
pool.explain: Many trees drop their leaves in autumn. In the short, cold winter days they stand bare until spring.
